sources.quote: ר״ל קול הברת לחם שעורים
sources.says: Ralbag says it means the sound made by the barley bread.

7:13.headline: Barley bread stands for weak Israel, or the Omer offering
7:13.body: Radak says the barley loaf is a picture of weak Israel overpowering Midian. Rashi says the barley recalls the merit of the Omer, the barley offering brought at Passover.

sources.quote: והיה זה משל על ישראל שהיו חלושים מתגברים על מדין ומנצחין אותם
sources.says: Radak says the dream is a parable for Israel, who were weak, overpowering Midian and defeating them.

sources.quote: הוּא זְכוּת הָעוֹמֶר הַקָּרֵב בְּפֶסַח
sources.says: Rashi says the barley bread is the merit of the Omer offering brought at Passover.

7:15.headline: A dream's meaning is its 'breaking', which opens it up
7:15.body: שבר can mean breaking or buying. Radak and Metzudat Zion say a dream is sealed shut and its meaning breaks it open, while Rashi glosses it as 'its sale'.

sources.quote: כי החלום הוא דבר סתום וסגור, ועל ידי הפתרון ישובר ויופתח
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means the interpretation, because a dream is sealed and closed, and the interpretation breaks it and opens it.

sources.quote: כי החלום כמו הדבר החתום והסתום והפתרון שובר אותו ומגלה אותו
sources.says: Radak says a dream is like a sealed thing, and the interpretation breaks it and reveals it.

sources.quote: וְאֶת מִמְכָּרוֹ, כְּלוֹמַר: וְאֶת פִּתְרוֹנוֹ
sources.says: Rashi glosses it as 'its sale', meaning its interpretation.

7:16.headline: Shofars and torches recall the giving of the Torah
7:16.body: Rashi says the shofars and torches call up the merit of the giving of the Torah. In the plain sense, it was night, so they carried torches and hid them in jars so the enemy would not see them.

sources.quote: שׁוֹפָרוֹת וְלַפִּידִים. לְהַזְכִּיר זְכוּת מַתַּן תּוֹרָה
sources.says: Rashi says the shofars and torches were to recall the merit of the giving of the Torah.

sources.quote: לְפִיכָךְ נָשְׂאוּ שָׁם לַפִּידִים לְהָאִיר לָהֶם וּנְתָנוּם בַּכַּדִּים כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יָבִינוּ בַּלַּפִּידִים
sources.says: Rashi says in the plain sense it was night, so they carried torches for light and put them in jars so the torches would not be noticed.

7:19.headline: The night watches are named for angels' shifts of song
7:19.body: The night was split into three watches. Metzudat Zion cites the Talmud that they are named for three groups of angels, each keeping its own time to sing.

sources.quote: ויקראו אשמורות על שם שנחלקה לשלשה כתות מלאכים, וכל כת שומר זמנו לומר בה שירה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the night has three parts, called watches because the angels are split into three groups, each keeping its time to sing.

7:21.headline: A cry of panic, or a war cry that set them fighting
7:21.body: Rashi and Radak say the Midianites shouted in fear as they fled. Malbim says some raised a war cry while others ran, so the shouters took the runners for the enemy and turned on them.

sources.quote: וַיָּרִיעוּ. תְּרוּעַת מַסָּע וְנִיסָה
sources.says: Rashi says it was a shout of moving off and fleeing.

sources.quote: ומה שאמר ויריעו תרועת שבר ופחד
sources.says: Radak says it was a shout of breaking and fear.

sources.quote: אז מקצתם הריעו תרועת מלחמה ומקצתם התחילו לנוס
sources.says: Malbim says some of them raised a war cry and some began to flee.

sources.quote: חשבו המריעים שהנסים הם אויביהם
sources.says: Malbim says the shouters thought those fleeing were their enemies.

8:2.headline: Gideon calms Ephraim with a picture of leftover grapes
8:2.body: עללות are the small grapes picked last, after the main harvest. Radak gives two readings: your weakest beat our best, or your late catch of the Midianite princes beats my whole battle.

sources.quote: הם הענבים הפחותים הנלקטים בסוף
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says עוללות are the lesser grapes gathered at the end.

sources.quote: דרך משל כלומר הפחותים שבכם טובים מהגדולים שבנו או עוללות ובציר משל על מדין
sources.says: Radak says it is a parable: either your lesser men beat our great ones, or the gleanings and the harvest stand for the war with Midian.

8:7.headline: Beat them with thorns, or throw them on thorns?
8:7.body: ודשתי means "I will thresh". Radak reads it as beating their flesh with thorns. He notes that the Targum reads it as throwing them on the thorns and trampling them.

sources.quote: ונראה מדבריו שפירושו שישליכם על הקוצים ערומים וידוש ברגליו עליהם
sources.says: Radak says the Targum seems to mean he would throw them naked on the thorns and trample them.

sources.quote: ואדוש ית בסריכון על כובי מדברא
sources.says: The Targum says "I will thresh your flesh on the thorns of the desert".

8:7.headline: A town called Sukkot, "thorns", is punished with thorns
8:7.body: Radak suggests Sukkot was a place full of thorns and got its name from them. He links it to a word for thorns in Job. So Gideon threatens them with thorns.

sources.quote: ונראה כי סכות זה היה מקום קוצים וברקנים לפיכך שם העיר סוכות כמו התמלא בסכות עורו שפירושו קוצים
sources.says: Radak says Sukkot seems to have been a place of thorns, which is why it was named Sukkot, like the word for thorns in Job.

8:13.headline: חרס, usually clay, here means the sun
8:13.body: Rashi, Radak and Metzudat Zion read החרס as the sun, as in Job. Rashi says Gideon came back before sunset. Radak also gives a reading where he came back at dawn.

sources.quote: החרס.} השמש, כמו (איוב ט ז) האומר לחרס ולא יזרח
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says החרס is the sun, as in Job: "who commands the sun and it does not rise".

sources.quote: עד שלא שקעה השמש
sources.says: Rashi says it means before the sun set.

sources.quote: ויש לפרש כי כל הלילה רדף גדעון אחרי זבח וצלמונע ובבקר כעלות השחר שב מן המלחמה
sources.says: Radak adds a reading that Gideon chased them all night and came back at dawn.

8:16.headline: Did Gideon "teach" Sukkot a lesson, or break them?
8:16.body: וידע looks like "he made known". The Targum and Radak read it as "he broke" them with thorns. Radak also allows the plain sense: he made their crime known to them.

sources.quote: כתרגומו ותבר עליהון מן וידוע חולי שהוא לשון שבירה ויתכן לפרשו כמשמעו שהודיע להם פשעם עם הקוצים
sources.says: Radak says it means "broke", as the Targum has it, but it may also mean that he made their sin known to them with the thorns.

sources.quote: וידע.} תרגם יונתן: ותבר
sources.says: Metzudat Zion notes that the Targum renders it "and he broke".

8:18.headline: Maimonides: תאר means outward shape, never said of God
8:18.body: The Guide for the Perplexed uses this verse to show that תאר means the visible outline of a thing. That is different from צלם, "image", and תאר is never used of God.

sources.quote: המונח המיוחד לה בעברית הוא "{תואר}"
sources.says: The Guide says the outward shape of a thing, as most people understand form, is called תואר in Hebrew, and cites "like the form of a king's sons".

sources.quote: המונח הזה אינו חל על האלוה יתעלה כלל
sources.says: The Guide says this word does not apply to God at all.

8:18.headline: One of them looked royal, or all of them did?
8:18.body: The Targum reads אחד as "one of them" who looked like a prince. Rashi and Radak also read it as "one look": all of them looked like you, like princes.

sources.quote: יונתן תרגם: אחד היה בהם שתוארו כתואר בני המלך
sources.says: Rashi says the Targum reads it as one among them who looked like a king's son, and that it can also mean they all had one look.

sources.quote: כמוך כמוהם צלם אחד וצורה אחת והיו כתואר בני המלך
sources.says: Radak reads it as one image and one form: they looked like you, like princes.

8:24.headline: Why are the Midianites suddenly called Ishmaelites?
8:24.body: Radak explains that Midian descends from Keturah, whom he identifies with Hagar, Ishmael's mother. He adds that the Targum may mean the Arab tent dwellers instead.

sources.quote: מדינים הם ישמעאלים כי בני קטורה הם וקטורה היא הגר
sources.says: Radak says the Midianites are Ishmaelites because they are Keturah's sons, and Keturah is Hagar.

sources.quote: אבל הערבים השכוני באהלים
sources.says: Radak says the Targum seems to refer instead to the Arabs who live in tents.

9:4.headline: Reckless men: פחז is 'haste' with its letters flipped
9:4.body: Rashi says פוחזים are men who rush to act without thinking. Metzudat Zion links it to 'unstable as water' in Genesis 49:4. He says the word is חפזון, haste, with its letters reversed.

sources.quote: בְּהוּלִים בְּמַעֲשֵׂיהֶם לַעֲשׂוֹת בְּלֹא תְבוּנָה
sources.says: Rashi says they were hasty in their deeds, acting without understanding.

sources.quote: מהירים במעשיהם מבלי דעת, כמו (בראשית מט ד) פחז כמים, והוא הפוך מן חפזון
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means rushing without thought, like 'unstable as water', and is חפזון with the letters turned around.

9:6.headline: אלון: not an oak here but a plain with a standing stone
9:6.body: אלון usually means an oak. Rashi and Radak follow the Targum, which reads it as a plain. The 'plain of the pillar' had a standing stone set up in it.

sources.quote: מֵישַׁר קָמְתָא - מִישׁוֹר שֶׁהָיוּ בּוֹ מַצֵּבוֹת
sources.says: Rashi cites the Targum: a plain that had standing stones in it.

sources.quote: ואלון מוצב כתרגומו מישר קמתא היתה אבן או זולתה מצב שם ויוחס המישור אליו
sources.says: Radak says it is a plain, named for a stone or something else set up there.

9:9.headline: How olive oil honors both God and people
9:9.body: The olive says its oil honors God and people. Metzudat David says oil lights the Temple lamp, which honors God. It also anoints priests and kings, which honors people.

sources.quote: כי בשמן זית מכבדים את המקום בנרות המנורה (שמות כז כ), ואת האנשים במשיחת הכהנים והמלכים
sources.says: Metzudat David says olive oil honors God in the menorah lamps and honors people in anointing priests and kings.

sources.quote: בנר שמדליקין בשמן זית לפני אלהים ולפני אנשים
sources.says: Radak says it is the lamp lit with olive oil before God and before people, or oil in offerings and in food.

9:11.headline: The fig's 'sweetness' is bee honey, and Deborah means bee
9:11.body: Rashi has said the fig is Deborah. Now he reads its sweetness as bee honey, דבש דבורים. The name דבורה is the Hebrew word for a bee.

sources.quote: אֶת מָתְקִי. דְּבַשׁ דְּבוֹרִים
sources.says: Rashi says 'my sweetness' means bee honey.

9:13.headline: Wine 'gladdens God'? The Targum will not say God feels joy
9:13.body: Rashi says wine gladdens God because the Levites sang only over the wine poured on the altar. The Aramaic Targum changes it to 'with it they pour offerings before God'. Radak says the Targum did this because God has no joy or sadness.

sources.quote: שֶׁאֵין אוֹמְרִים הַלְוִיִּם שִׁיר שֶׁל הַקָּרְבָּן אֶלָּא עַל הַנְּסָכִים
sources.says: Rashi says the Levites sang the offering song only over the wine libations.

sources.quote: דְמִנֵיהּ מְנַסְכִין קֳדָם יְיָ
sources.says: The Targum renders it 'from which they pour libations before the Lord'.

sources.quote: הרחיק יונתן ע"ה השמחה מהבורא יתעלה כמו שהרחיק כל שאר התארים ממנו כי אין לפניו לא שמחה ולא עצבון
sources.says: Radak says the Targum kept joy away from God, as it does with other such traits, because God has neither joy nor sadness.

9:15.headline: 'Shelter in my shade', says a bush that has no shade
9:15.body: The thornbush invites the tall cedars to rest in its shade. Malbim points out that a thornbush has no shade at all. Metzudat David softens it: the little shade it has.

sources.quote: וידוע שהאטד אין לו צל כלל והוא השפל מכולם
sources.says: Malbim says it is known that the thornbush has no shade at all and is the lowest of them all.

sources.quote: במעט הצל שיש בי אהיה עליכם למחסה
sources.says: Metzudat David says it means 'with the little shade I have, I will shelter you'.

9:22.headline: Abimelech 'ruled', and the verse will not say he 'judged'
9:22.body: וישר means he held power. Radak and Malbim note that the verse does not say וישפט, he judged, as it does for real judges. Rashi says he ruled them against their will, with pride.

sources.quote: לפיכך אמר וישר ולא אמר וישפוט כי לא הלך בדרך טובה ולא החזיר את ישראל למוטב
sources.says: Radak says the verse says 'ruled' and not 'judged' because he did not walk a good path or bring Israel back to good.

sources.quote: עַל כָּרְחָם נָהַג רַבָּנוּת וּבְגַאֲוָה
sources.says: Rashi says he lorded over them against their will and with arrogance.

sources.quote: לא כתיב וישפט, כי לא שפט רק שר בחזקה
sources.says: Malbim says it does not say 'judged', because he did not judge but ruled by force.

9:31.headline: A 'siege' from inside: they are closing the city to you
9:31.body: צרים usually means to besiege a city from outside. Radak and Metzudat David say here it means the opposite. Gaal's men are guarding the city from inside so Abimelech cannot get in.

sources.quote: כן נקרא מצור כששומרים את העיר שלא יכנס אדם בה מבחוץ
sources.says: Radak says it is also called a siege when the city is guarded so no one from outside can enter.

sources.quote: מפתים אנשי העיר לעשות העיר מצור בעבורך שלא תכנוס בה
sources.says: Metzudat David says Gaal is persuading the city to shut itself against Abimelech so he cannot enter.

9:53.headline: The 'rider' is the upper millstone that rides on the lower one
9:53.body: רכב usually means a chariot. Rashi and Metzudat Zion say here it is the upper millstone. Radak says it is called the rider because it sits on the lower stone.

sources.quote: חֲתִיכַת אֶבֶן שֶׁל רֵחַיִם הָעֶלְיוֹנָה הַקְּרוּיָה רֶכֶב
sources.says: Rashi says it was a piece of the upper millstone, which is called רכב.

sources.quote: הוא האבן העליון מהרחיים, הרוכב על התחתית
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it is the upper millstone, which rides on the lower one.

sources.quote: והיא העליונה לפיכך נקראת רכב
sources.says: Radak says it is the upper stone, and that is why it is called רכב.
